about: AAFDID has not published an Acquisition of Services requirements table. These entries were drawn on 2026-09-30 from DoDI 5000.74, Defense Acquisition of Services (January 10, 2020, Change 1 effective June 24, 2021), the AAF services pages, and DFARS 207.103 for the written acquisition plan threshold. Each entry cites its paragraph. DoDI 5000.74 still uses pre-2022 Title 10 section numbers; the renumbered section is noted where AAFDID's Title 10 crosswalk gives one.

scat.label: Special Interest
scat.rule: Designated by ASD(A); no dollar threshold

scat.label: S-CAT I
scat.rule: $1B or more total, or more than $300M in any one year
scat.decision_authority: Service or component acquisition executive, or designee

scat.label: S-CAT II
scat.decision_authority: Service or component acquisition executive, or designee

scat.label: S-CAT III
scat.decision_authority: Component Senior Services Manager or designee

scat.label: S-CAT IV
scat.decision_authority: Component Senior Services Manager or designee

scat.label: S-CAT V
scat.rule: Above the simplified acquisition threshold, but less than $10M
scat.decision_authority: Component Senior Services Manager or designee

scat_cite: DoDI 5000.74, para 3.5.a and Table 1; thresholds use the IGCE in current-year dollars (Table 1, note 1)

requirements.name: Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE)
requirements.note: The IGCE in current-year dollars sets the services category (S-CAT), and with it the decision authority.

requirements.name: Functional Services Manager (FSM) designation and multi-functional team
requirements.approval: The requiring activity designates the FSM
requirements.note: The FSM leads a multi-functional team and develops the preferred solution: initial acquisition strategy, business approach, assumptions, risks and cost.

requirements.name: Market research, documented
requirements.note: Identify providers by competency, performance and cost, and maximize reliance on the commercial marketplace. Initial market research informs the SRRB.

requirements.name: Requirement cost analysis
requirements.note: An analysis of the discrete costs within the service requirement, paired with initial market research, so the SRRB can weigh mission need, cost and affordability.

requirements.name: Services Requirements Review Board (SRRB) validation and approval
requirements.source: DoDI 5000.74, paras 4.3.a-c and 4.3.e-f; FY2011 NDAA sec. 863 (per the AAFDID AoS overview)
requirements.approval: SRRB chair in the requiring organization
requirements.applies_when: Total estimated value of $10M or more. For IDIQs, the base contract and any task order of $10M or more.
requirements.note: The SRRB reviews, validates, prioritizes and approves the requirement before the procurement request goes to contracting. It considers mission need, alignment, risks, related requirements, workforce, projected cost through the FYDP, sensitive functions and metrics (para 4.3.g).

requirements.name: Workforce analysis: insource or outsource
requirements.approval: SRRB chair, coordinated with component manpower officials
requirements.applies_when: Reviewed at the SRRB: total estimated value of $10M or more.
requirements.note: Explain why military or civilian personnel cannot do the work. The Director, Office of Small Business Programs, reviews any decision to convert small-business work to federal employees (para 1.2.c(4)).

requirements.name: Review and justification of critical functions and functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions
requirements.source: DoDI 5000.74, paras 1.2.c and 4.3.g(8); 10 U.S.C. 2330a(e) as cited (now 10 U.S.C. 4505, per AAFDID's Title 10 crosswalk); FAR 7.503(e); DFARS 207.503
requirements.applies_when: Contractors will perform critical functions or functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions.
requirements.note: Reliance on contractors for these functions must be reviewed, justified, and reduced to the maximum extent practicable.

requirements.name: Services Acquisition Workshop (SAW)
requirements.approval: Waiver by the component Senior Services Manager; for Special Interest acquisitions, by the decision authority
requirements.applies_when: Total value of $500M or more, or $250M or more in a year. For a multiple-award IDIQ, not the base award, but any task order of $100M or more.
requirements.note: The team completes a SAW, or an equivalent, before the acquisition strategy is approved.

requirements.name: Business case analysis for requirements that overlap existing vehicles
requirements.approval: Required by the component Portfolio Manager; approver not stated
requirements.applies_when: $50M or more, with potential significant overlap with an existing contract, a DoD or government-wide vehicle, or a best-in-class contract.

requirements.name: Acquisition strategy as a written acquisition plan
requirements.approval: Decision authority for the S-CAT (DoDI 5000.74, Table 1)
requirements.applies_when: Total cost of all contracts of $50M or more, or $25M or more in any fiscal year (DFARS 207.103(d)(i)(B)).
requirements.note: Content follows DFARS 207.105, with enough detail for the decision authority to judge business sense, compliance with law and policy, and affordability.

requirements.name: Acquisition strategy in streamlined documentation
requirements.approval: Decision authority for the S-CAT (DoDI 5000.74, Table 1)
requirements.applies_when: Below the written acquisition plan threshold: under $50M total and under $25M in every fiscal year.
requirements.note: Covers requirements development, acquisition planning, solicitation and award, significant risks, contract and performance management, and the metrics evaluation plan, including a summary of the analysis of alternatives.

requirements.name: Small business participation opportunities
requirements.note: Opportunities for small businesses, including socio-economic concerns, as prime contractors and subcontractors.

requirements.name: Performance-based approach and contract type rationale
requirements.note: Use performance-based services acquisition or explain why not, and give a rationale for any contract type other than firm-fixed-price.

requirements.name: Intellectual property management mechanisms
requirements.note: Identify and manage IP so that government and industry get a fair return and a follow-on provider can take over competitively.

requirements.name: Rationale and authority for other than full and open competition
requirements.applies_when: Only if other than full and open competition is planned.

requirements.name: Consolidation or bundling summary, coordinated with the Office of Small Business Programs
requirements.applies_when: Only if the requirement is consolidated or bundled.

requirements.name: Contract line items with Product or Service Codes
requirements.note: Line items follow FAR 4.1005, including the required Product or Service Code.

requirements.name: Performance management metrics
requirements.note: Tailored metrics that signal cost, schedule, performance, small business and competition risk, and inform renewals and re-competes.

requirements.name: FSM cost and metrics tracking, with deviation notice
requirements.approval: Notice goes to the requiring activity
requirements.note: The FSM tracks performance against cost targets and immediately notifies the requiring activity of significant cost, schedule or performance deviations.

requirements.name: Trained and qualified contracting officer's representative (COR)
SRRB validation before exercising an option
requirements.applies_when: Acquisitions under SRRB review: $10M or more.

requirements.name: Independent management reviews (post-award)
requirements.source: DoDI 5000.74, para 4.6.a; 10 U.S.C. 2330 as cited (now 10 U.S.C. 4501)
requirements.applies_when: Post-award contracts with a total value of $100M or more, and others the component chooses.
requirements.note: Periodic reviews of contract performance, contracting mechanisms, subcontractor management, oversight staffing and pass-through charges.

requirements.name: Review of contracts where a contractor oversees other contractors
requirements.applies_when: Only if one contractor oversees services performed by other contractors.
requirements.note: Reviews reliance on the contractor for functions closely associated with inherently governmental functions, and the prime's financial interest in the work it oversees.

requirements.name: Bridge contract status update and notifications
requirements.approval: Requirements owner and contracting officer send the update; routing depends on the $10M threshold
requirements.applies_when: A bridge contract is used because of inadequate planning, as the S-CAT decision authority determines. Contingency, humanitarian and disaster-response actions are excluded.
requirements.note: First use: a status update with the rationale. A second use under $10M: notice to the armed force's Vice Chief of Staff and the service acquisition executive or agency head. Plan early enough to avoid bridges.
